The opening name and fuller genealogy remain Heilprin’s compressed presentation. The checked Kohelet story identifies the unnamed son only. The grandson form is reported in the Arukh by Etz Yosef. Neither establishes the full heading’s chain.

The exact Arukh edition and Eikhah attribution are unresolved. The modern headword search did not recover the reported wording. Etz Yosef independently transmits the grandson variant, and both relevant midrash passages were checked.

The explanation of how the Arukh came to conflate the stories remains Heilprin’s inference. Kohelet directly places the stories together, and the Eikhah section gives the second one. The checked passages do not establish the lexicographer’s process.
